Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) announces two new rugged laptops, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14, purpose-built for field workers who need technology that performs in the harshest conditions. From utility technicians troubleshooting infrastructure in extreme weather to public safety officers coordinating response efforts in the field, both devices are designed to keep workers productive when conditions are most demanding.
Managing a fleet of devices across distributed field operations demands technology that won't let workers down. Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 give IT teams a standardized, manageable platform that combines field-grade durability, AI-ready performance and advanced connectivity for large-scale field deployments.
Designed for workers across federal and local government, public safety, manufacturing, oil and gas, transportation and utilities, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are built to perform in the most demanding conditions. They are MIL-STD-810H certified for proven reliability with a temperature range of -20°F to 145°F, covering virtually any climate field workers might face. Displays feature gloved and water multitouch support for use in personal protective equipment or wet conditions.
Both laptops are powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors that offload AI and background tasks, keeping the system responsive during long shifts. They offer optional private 5G, Wi-Fi 7 and GPS for reliable connectivity and location tracking in remote locations. Hot-swappable batteries help ensure uninterrupted productivity for even the longest shifts. With up to a 5MP RGB+IR camera available on both laptops, workers can capture high-quality images and video in any environment.
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are equipped with Rugged Control Center, built-in software that makes critical device settings easily accessible. From GPS module configuration to custom hardware shortcuts and device customization, it gives field workers the control they need to tailor their devices to the demands of the job.
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme: Maximum durability in the smallest footprint
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme is the most powerful and smallest 13-inch fully rugged AI PC. Built for the harshest environments, it carries an IP66 rating for full protection against dust and water ingress and has been drop-tested from six feet.
Performance: Intel Arc integrated graphics support visual and data-heavy workflows and up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X memory offers responsive performance for heavy multitasking. Removable SSD and self-encrypting drive options give organizations control over security and compliance in sensitive environments.
Display experience: The 13.3-inch FHD display reaches 1,400 nits of brightness for full readability in direct sunlight.
Dell Pro Rugged 14: Professional-grade performance for field work
Dell Pro Rugged 14 is built for professionals who need advanced performance in a portable, field-ready form factor. It's the smallest and most powerful 14-inch semi-rugged AI PC, weighing approximately 4.7 pounds, yet durable enough for field work with three-foot drop protection and an IP-53 rating for protection against dust, dirt and water exposure.
Performance: With an NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 Blackwell Generation Laptop GPU, users can support demanding visualization, data analysis and AI workloads in the field. LPCAMM2 memory up to 64 GB makes it easier for IT teams to upgrade or swap memory modules.
Display experience: The 14-inch 16:10 FHD display delivers up to 1,100 nits of brightness with a wider aspect ratio for reviewing documents, data dashboards and field applications.
Vehicle docking: Redesigned vehicle docking with quad passthrough provides enhanced connectivity and compatibility with third-party docking solutions, and an improved user experience makes it easy to dock and undock, ideal for workers who operate primarily from the road.
New Dell Pro Rugged laptops include Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0, contacted and contactless smart card readers, fingerprint readers and IR cameras for Windows Hello facial recognition. Dell SafeID with ControlVault and BIOS-level defenses make these laptops the world's most secure rugged PCs, now further hardened with quantum-resistant protections. For IT teams managing large fleets, the laptops support cloud-based deployment, management and security tools, backed by Dell ProSupport and predictive maintenance tools to minimize downtime.
Charlie Walker"Field workers keep critical operations running no matter the conditions, and their technology needs to do the same. Our new Dell Pro Rugged laptops deliver the performance, durability and connectivity that keep workers productive when it matters most, with the standardization and security IT teams need for small to large-scale deployments."
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 will be available in early October.

How AI Server Demand Will Impact Dell Stock Investors
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:10 AM CDT 4 min read
Recent announcements show Dell Technologies supplying AI infrastructure and expertise to partners such as Honeywell and Accenture, while rolling out AI focused PCs, workstations and data platforms aimed at on premises and edge workloads.
The scale of AI server orders, large backlog and expanding partnerships indicates that Dell Technologies is increasingly embedded in customers' long term AI infrastructure plans.

Dell Technologies Investment Narrative Recap
To own Dell Technologies today, you need to believe its AI infrastructure push can keep converting that US$130b order book and US$95b backlog into shipped systems without eroding overall profitability. The key near term swing factor is execution, specifically getting constrained components and services wrapped around AI servers so mix and margins hold up rather than slide.
The biggest risk still sits in hardware economics. AI GPU servers run at mid single digit operating margins, which can dilute returns if storage, services and PCs do not pull their weight. Recent alliances and product launches do not remove that risk yet, but they do give Dell Technologies more routes to attach higher value software and data platforms.
Among the latest announcements, the expanded partnership with Accenture is the one to watch for near term catalysts. The new Accenture Dell Business Group is built around on premises AI factories, private AI stacks and lifecycle services, which line up directly with the large AI server and storage backlog that Dell Technologies is already carrying.
Execution here matters. If Accenture can train more than 3,000 practitioners on the Dell portfolio and push integrated AI infrastructure into regulated industries, that supports higher services attachment and better use of Dell Technologies' AI Data Platform and servers. It also helps offset some of the risk from commodity hardware pressure and tight supply, though it does not remove those pressures.
Dell Technologies AI Story Through The Numbers
Dell Technologies' current analyst narrative points to US$266.7b in revenue and US$20.8b in earnings by 2029, built on an assumed 20.8% yearly revenue growth rate and a move from US$11.4b in earnings today to that 2029 consensus figure. This would require an earnings increase of about US$9.4b over the period.

The most cautious analysts only had 2029 revenue around US$215.6b and earnings of US$16.4b before this news, a much cooler story. That gap in expectations shows how widely opinions can differ, so it makes sense to compare multiple narratives before deciding how this new alliance might reshape your own outlook.

Efosa Obano Walked Away From His Career At Dell Technologies To Support Black Canadian Founders
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 11:41 AM CDT 4 min read
At the University of Toronto (U of T), a vision aims to support Black entrepreneurs nationwide.
Efosa KC Obano is an alumnus of the university who moved to Canada from Lagos, Nigeria, in 2013 to study strategic management.
He arrived in Canada when there were nearly 300,000 Africans in the country, a number, he said, that has grown to over 1.5 million. That motivated him to serve as director of marketing and external relations for the university's African Students Association, supporting second- and third-generation immigrants.
that his upbringing shaped his decision to pursue entrepreneurship as it could be a "means of social change." Having grown up without access to internet or 24/7 electricity, he saw how companies or entrepreneurs created such access for people.
He founded the African Impact Initiative in 2018, which funds and supports African entrepreneurs building in Canada and across Africa. The University of Toronto invested in the organization. Obano also spent three and a half years at Dell Technologies, helping champion small businesses with Dell's infrastructure and leading the social impact portfolio. His time there overlapped with the period following George Floyd's death in 2020.
"Every organization is like trying to think, 'OK, what can we do better to support Black entrepreneurs or Black people in general?' Because U of T supported me with my first organization, the African Impact Initiative, I was one of the few Black founders at the time that they had supported with anything sort of financial," he told AFROTECH
. "So, they had reached out to ask, 'What can we do to help Black entrepreneurs here?' My other organization at the time had blown up, lots of awards, lots of recognition, etc., but that was in Africa. And they were the sponsors, so they were seeing all that success and they were like, 'Is there a community of folks here that are also building that we can support?'"
Obano spent the year speaking with as many Black entrepreneurs in Canada as possible to learn about the barriers they faced. To his surprise, the biggest barrier wasn't capital, it was community. People wanted to build around those who understood their lived experience.
That year, Obano received his permanent residency and took a pay cut from his senior salaried role at Dell Technologies to make an impact beyond financial wealth. In October 2021, the Black Founders Network (BFN) launched. It is an inclusive community for Black founders at all stages, with support, networks, resources, and the capacity to scale.
BFN provides access to capital across three key stages, beginning with Core, which helps aspiring entrepreneurs through introductory sessions on ideation, startup development, and team building. Participants also receive monthly office hours, co-working space at U of T's Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, and a chance to win $4,000 CAD through the Smart Start Awards to develop their MVP (minimal viable product), according to the website.
At the Accelerate stage, founders have built their MVP. They may have some early revenue and a waitlist. BFN supports them in boosting users and revenue by providing up to $25,000 in funding grants, along with cohort-based programming, Obana said. They can also build alongside the best founders through its alum base.
Founders earning at least $250,000 in annual revenue qualify for the next stage, Scale, and will receive help raising seed rounds and, in some cases, Series A rounds. They also can receive $50,000 and more in grants. Obano said Scale will help them expand into new markets.
BFN further offers a career advancement program that trains and connects the BFN network's best-performing talent with companies that want to hire them. He noted that sometimes founders in his program realize they would rather work for someone else than build their own companies. BFN awards grants to companies to hire from this talent pool.
Additionally, the BE Her program addresses the unique challenges Black women entrepreneurs face.
Over the past five years, BFN's programming has served more than 15,000 people. Success stories include OneCliq, an AI-powered culture-context insights engine co-founded by siblings Nathan Knight and Tanika McLeod, which Dig Insights acquired in July 2025.
Knight and McLeod now mentor for BFN's programs and have also invested in some of its companies.
BFN has more than $200 million in financial value, and Obano said this reflects its companies' revenues and the funds they've raised.
Looking ahead, he added that a Black Founders Fund is in the works to create more funding pathways, and he is in talks with well-resourced, credible universities to replicate the work they have done with the University of Toronto.

Why Is Dell Technologies (DELL) Up 9.3% Since Last Earnings Report?
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Dell Technologies (DELL). Shares have added about 9.3% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.
Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Dell Technologies due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for Dell Technologies Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
DELL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong AI Demand Aids Revenue Growth
Dell Technologies reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $7.04 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 41.65%. The company reported earnings of $2.32 per share in the year-ago quarter.
Revenues surged 58% to $46.97 billion and beat the consensus mark by 8.57%. Broad-based infrastructure demand drove the quarterly results, while AI server orders reached a record $60.9 billion.
DELL's ISG Growth Accelerates Across the Portfolio
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) revenues jumped 89% year over year to a record $31.78 billion. AI-optimized server revenues doubled to $16.4 billion, while traditional servers and networking revenues surged 122% year over year to $10.53 billion. Dell exited the quarter with $95 billion of AI backlog, while its opportunity pipeline remained multiples of backlog.
Storage revenues increased 26% year over year to $4.85 billion as Dell IP demand grew above the market for a sixth consecutive quarter.
ISG operating income jumped 225% year over year to $4.78 billion, with operating margin expanding 620 basis points (bps) on a year-over-year basis to 15%. Dell also said its AI customer base surpassed 6,500 across neocloud, sovereign and enterprise customers.
Dell's Server Refresh Opportunity Supports Demand
Dell said traditional server demand reflects data-center modernization, security and resiliency requirements, and rising CPU needs tied to AI and agentic workloads. The company still has roughly 1.2 million installed assets running 14th-generation or older servers, leaving a sizable refresh opportunity as customers upgrade infrastructure.
Dell also highlighted significant consolidation benefits from newer systems. Seventeenth-generation servers can replace five to seven legacy servers, while 18th-generation systems can replace up to 13. The newer platforms also offer higher processing density and better power efficiency, supporting modernization even as industry supply remains constrained.
Dell's CSG Posts Broad-Based Revenue Growth
Client Solutions Group (CSG) revenues increased 20% year over year to $15.03 billion. Commercial revenues rose 22% year over year to $13.19 billion, marking the eighth straight quarter of growth, while consumer revenues advanced 7% to $1.84 billion. Demand grew across all regions and verticals, led by large-enterprise PC refresh activity.
CSG operating income increased 42% year over year to $1.14 billion. The operating margin improved 120 bps to 7.6%, supported by pricing discipline and greater scale.
Dell said it will continue balancing demand with product availability as it pursues profitable share gains in the client business.
DELL Expands Profitability Through Scale and Mix
Non-GAAP gross margin rose 78% year over year to $9.93 billion, while the gross margin improved to 21.1% from 18.7%.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 22% year over year to $4 billion but fell to 8.5% of revenues from 11% a year earlier, reflecting meaningful operating leverage.
That expense leverage helped non-GAAP operating income surge 160% year over year to $5.93 billion. The operating margin expanded to 12.6% from 7.7%, aided by higher revenue scale, pricing discipline and improved storage profitability.
Management tied part of the storage improvement to a higher mix of Dell IP products and better rates across solutions.
DELL Delivers Strong Cash Flow and Capital Returns
As of July 31, 2026, DELL has $14.248 billion in cash and investments and a core leverage ratio of 0.8 times. The company reported $14.062 billion in cash and investments as of May 1.
Cash flow from operations totaled $2.23 billion in the reported quarter, while adjusted free cash flow reached $8.15 billion.
Dell returned a record $4.3 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, underscoring the cash generation from higher profitability and revenue scale. Dell repurchased 9.5 million shares at an average price of $401 per share and paid a quarterly dividend of about 63 cents per share.
Dell Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue and Earnings Outlook
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Dell expects revenues of $49 billion, plus or minus $500 million, and non-GAAP earnings of $6.50 per share, plus or minus 10 cents.
DELL expects ISG revenues to grow roughly 145%, supported by about $19 billion in AI server revenues, while CSG revenues are expected to rise roughly 15%.
For fiscal 2027, Dell raised its revenue outlook by $25 billion to $192 billion, plus or minus $2 billion, and lifted non-GAAP earnings guidance to $25.50 per share, plus or minus 25 cents.
AI server revenues are now expected to reach $74 billion, or roughly three times the prior-year level, with traditional server growth forecast at just over 100%.
How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

The consensus estimate has shifted 48.54% due to these changes.

The refocused approach includes generative AI search tools and autonomous AI agents aimed at efficiency, cost control, and faster deployment cycles.

For a wider lens on where AI buildout is heading, compare Dell's approach with the broader set of companies building core infrastructure through 84 AI infrastructure stocks.
Dell Technologies operates as a global tech supplier that designs and supports hardware, software, and integrated solutions across multiple regions. A tighter AI roadmap directly affects how its servers, storage, and enterprise services can plug into customers' existing infrastructure decisions.
Does the team leading Dell Technologies have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.
What exactly has John Roese changed inside Dell Technologies?
Roese cut Dell's AI portfolio from about 900 projects to fewer than 100 and tied each one to a hard outcome such as revenue, profit, cost, or regulatory risk. That kind of pruning reduces duplicated effort and pushes product teams to focus on AI tools, like search and autonomous agents, that have clear payoffs for enterprise customers.
Does this recognition change the Dell Technologies Narrative investors have been using?
The Narrative already leans on rising enterprise AI demand, more tailored offerings, and a mix shift toward higher margin storage and services. Roese's AI reset lines up with that, because it concentrates resources on enterprise AI workloads that can support revenue visibility while still leaving the long running risks around hardware commoditization and the cyclical PC business in place.
See how these catalysts shape Dell Technologies' path to a $564 fair value.
What should investors watch next to judge whether this AI refocus is working?
The clearest test is how Dell's AI heavy infrastructure and services performance compares with the analyst framework that points to revenue of about US$265.3b and earnings of roughly US$20.5b by 2029. Progress toward those earnings and margin assumptions will indicate whether this refocused AI playbook is aligning with the financial profile analysts have mapped out.

Before you treat Dell Technologies as just an AI story, there is a quieter question to answer about what its future cash generation suggests the whole business might be worth versus today's share price. Find out exactly what Dell Technologies is worth today based on its cash flows.

Dell Technologies Introduces New Pro Rugged Laptops
Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) announces two new rugged laptops, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14, purpose-built for field workers who need technology that performs in the harshest conditions. From utility technicians troubleshooting infrastructure in extreme weather to public safety officers coordinating response efforts in the field, both devices are designed to keep workers productive when conditions are most demanding.
Managing a fleet of devices across distributed field operations demands technology that won't let workers down. Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 give IT teams a standardized, manageable platform that combines field-grade durability, AI-ready performance and advanced connectivity for large-scale field deployments.
Designed for workers across federal and local government, public safety, manufacturing, oil and gas, transportation and utilities, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are built to perform in the most demanding conditions. They are MIL-STD-810H certified for proven reliability with a temperature range of -20°F to 145°F, covering virtually any climate field workers might face. Displays feature gloved and water multitouch support for use in personal protective equipment or wet conditions.
Both laptops are powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors that offload AI and background tasks, keeping the system responsive during long shifts. They offer optional private 5G, Wi-Fi 7 and GPS for reliable connectivity and location tracking in remote locations. Hot-swappable batteries help ensure uninterrupted productivity for even the longest shifts. With up to a 5MP RGB+IR camera available on both laptops, workers can capture high-quality images and video in any environment.
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are equipped with Rugged Control Center, built-in software that makes critical device settings easily accessible. From GPS module configuration to custom hardware shortcuts and device customization, it gives field workers the control they need to tailor their devices to the demands of the job.
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme: Maximum durability in the smallest footprint
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme is the most powerful and smallest 13-inch fully rugged AI PC. Built for the harshest environments, it carries an IP66 rating for full protection against dust and water ingress and has been drop-tested from six feet.
Performance: Intel Arc integrated graphics support visual and data-heavy workflows and up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X memory offers responsive performance for heavy multitasking. Removable SSD and self-encrypting drive options give organizations control over security and compliance in sensitive environments.
Display experience: The 13.3-inch FHD display reaches 1,400 nits of brightness for full readability in direct sunlight.
Dell Pro Rugged 14: Professional-grade performance for field work
Dell Pro Rugged 14 is built for professionals who need advanced performance in a portable, field-ready form factor. It's the smallest and most powerful 14-inch semi-rugged AI PC, weighing approximately 4.7 pounds, yet durable enough for field work with three-foot drop protection and an IP-53 rating for protection against dust, dirt and water exposure.
Performance: With an NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 Blackwell Generation Laptop GPU, users can support demanding visualization, data analysis and AI workloads in the field. LPCAMM2 memory up to 64 GB makes it easier for IT teams to upgrade or swap memory modules.
Display experience: The 14-inch 16:10 FHD display delivers up to 1,100 nits of brightness with a wider aspect ratio for reviewing documents, data dashboards and field applications.
Vehicle docking: Redesigned vehicle docking with quad passthrough provides enhanced connectivity and compatibility with third-party docking solutions, and an improved user experience makes it easy to dock and undock, ideal for workers who operate primarily from the road.
New Dell Pro Rugged laptops include Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0, contacted and contactless smart card readers, fingerprint readers and IR cameras for Windows Hello facial recognition. Dell SafeID with ControlVault and BIOS-level defenses make these laptops the world's most secure rugged PCs, now further hardened with quantum-resistant protections. For IT teams managing large fleets, the laptops support cloud-based deployment, management and security tools, backed by Dell ProSupport and predictive maintenance tools to minimize downtime.
Charlie Walker"Field workers keep critical operations running no matter the conditions, and their technology needs to do the same. Our new Dell Pro Rugged laptops deliver the performance, durability and connectivity that keep workers productive when it matters most, with the standardization and security IT teams need for small to large-scale deployments."
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 will be available in early October.

Susquehanna has reiterated its Positive rating on Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) and maintained a $700 price target.
The updated Dell price target implies approximately 28% upside from the stock’s current price of about $543, according to a September 29 analyst note.
Analyst Mehdi Hosseini pointed to growing demand for AI inferencing as a key catalyst for Dell’s server business. Susquehanna expects traditional server revenue to double in fiscal 2027 before continuing to grow at a double-digit compound annual growth rate through fiscal 2029.
According to the analyst, enterprise customers and neocloud service providers are increasing spending on computing infrastructure needed for AI inferencing applications.
This trend is expected to drive further growth across Dell’s server segment and support upside to fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 estimates.
Hosseini noted that inferencing is becoming an increasingly important demand driver for original equipment manufacturers such as Dell, helping sustain growth beyond the initial wave of AI training deployments.
Meanwhile, Wall Street’s broader outlook on Dell remains constructive. TradingView data shows a consensus 12-month Dell stock forecast of approximately $595, representing modest upside from current levels.
Among the more bullish projections, Susquehanna’s $700 target ranks near the top of Wall Street estimates, while some analysts have issued targets as high as $735. Current analyst ratings remain concentrated in the ‘Buy’ and ‘Strong Buy’ categories.
DELL 12-month stock price prediction. Source: TradingView
The latest analyst update follows a strong year for Dell, which has emerged as a major beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom.
In its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results reported on September 1, Dell posted record revenue of $47 billion, up 58% year-over-year. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share came in at $7.04, representing growth of 203% from the same period last year.
AI-optimized servers remained the primary growth driver. Dell reported record AI server orders of $60.9 billion during the quarter and exited the period with a record AI backlog of $95 billion. Revenue from AI servers reached $16.4 billion, up 100% from a year earlier.
The company also raised its full-year fiscal 2027 guidance, projecting revenue of $192 billion and AI server revenue of $74 billion as AI infrastructure demand continues to accelerate.
Overall, Dell shares have delivered significant gains over the past year as investors increasingly bet on the company’s role in the expanding AI infrastructure market.
However, analysts continue to monitor AI spending trends, execution of the company’s large backlog, and broader volatility across the AI hardware sector.

How AI Server Demand Will Impact Dell Stock Investors
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:10 AM CDT 4 min read
Recent announcements show Dell Technologies supplying AI infrastructure and expertise to partners such as Honeywell and Accenture, while rolling out AI focused PCs, workstations and data platforms aimed at on premises and edge workloads.
The scale of AI server orders, large backlog and expanding partnerships indicates that Dell Technologies is increasingly embedded in customers' long term AI infrastructure plans.
Next, the focus shifts to how Dell Technologies' AI alliances and order backlog may reshape the existing investment narrative and risk balance.
Scan Dell Technologies' AI build out against other potential movers by checking the hand picked 55 AI infrastructure stocks that is now shaping the next wave of data center demand.
Dell Technologies Investment Narrative Recap
To own Dell Technologies today, you need to believe its AI infrastructure push can keep converting that US$130b order book and US$95b backlog into shipped systems without eroding overall profitability. The key near term swing factor is execution, specifically getting constrained components and services wrapped around AI servers so mix and margins hold up rather than slide.
The biggest risk still sits in hardware economics. AI GPU servers run at mid single digit operating margins, which can dilute returns if storage, services and PCs do not pull their weight. Recent alliances and product launches do not remove that risk yet, but they do give Dell Technologies more routes to attach higher value software and data platforms.
Among the latest announcements, the expanded partnership with Accenture is the one to watch for near term catalysts. The new Accenture Dell Business Group is built around on premises AI factories, private AI stacks and lifecycle services, which line up directly with the large AI server and storage backlog that Dell Technologies is already carrying.
Execution here matters. If Accenture can train more than 3,000 practitioners on the Dell portfolio and push integrated AI infrastructure into regulated industries, that supports higher services attachment and better use of Dell Technologies' AI Data Platform and servers. It also helps offset some of the risk from commodity hardware pressure and tight supply, though it does not remove those pressures.

Efosa Obano Walked Away From His Career At Dell Technologies To Support Black Canadian Founders
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 11:41 AM CDT 4 min read
At the University of Toronto (U of T), a vision aims to support Black entrepreneurs nationwide.
Efosa KC Obano is an alumnus of the university who moved to Canada from Lagos, Nigeria, in 2013 to study strategic management.
He arrived in Canada when there were nearly 300,000 Africans in the country, a number, he said, that has grown to over 1.5 million. That motivated him to serve as director of marketing and external relations for the university's African Students Association, supporting second- and third-generation immigrants.
that his upbringing shaped his decision to pursue entrepreneurship as it could be a "means of social change." Having grown up without access to internet or 24/7 electricity, he saw how companies or entrepreneurs created such access for people.
He founded the African Impact Initiative in 2018, which funds and supports African entrepreneurs building in Canada and across Africa. The University of Toronto invested in the organization. Obano also spent three and a half years at Dell Technologies, helping champion small businesses with Dell's infrastructure and leading the social impact portfolio. His time there overlapped with the period following George Floyd's death in 2020.
"Every organization is like trying to think, 'OK, what can we do better to support Black entrepreneurs or Black people in general?' Because U of T supported me with my first organization, the African Impact Initiative, I was one of the few Black founders at the time that they had supported with anything sort of financial," he told AFROTECH
. "So, they had reached out to ask, 'What can we do to help Black entrepreneurs here?' My other organization at the time had blown up, lots of awards, lots of recognition, etc., but that was in Africa. And they were the sponsors, so they were seeing all that success and they were like, 'Is there a community of folks here that are also building that we can support?'"
Obano spent the year speaking with as many Black entrepreneurs in Canada as possible to learn about the barriers they faced. To his surprise, the biggest barrier wasn't capital, it was community. People wanted to build around those who understood their lived experience.
That year, Obano received his permanent residency and took a pay cut from his senior salaried role at Dell Technologies to make an impact beyond financial wealth. In October 2021, the Black Founders Network (BFN) launched. It is an inclusive community for Black founders at all stages, with support, networks, resources, and the capacity to scale.
BFN provides access to capital across three key stages, beginning with Core, which helps aspiring entrepreneurs through introductory sessions on ideation, startup development, and team building. Participants also receive monthly office hours, co-working space at U of T's Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, and a chance to win $4,000 CAD through the Smart Start Awards to develop their MVP (minimal viable product), according to the website.
At the Accelerate stage, founders have built their MVP. They may have some early revenue and a waitlist. BFN supports them in boosting users and revenue by providing up to $25,000 in funding grants, along with cohort-based programming, Obana said. They can also build alongside the best founders through its alum base.
Founders earning at least $250,000 in annual revenue qualify for the next stage, Scale, and will receive help raising seed rounds and, in some cases, Series A rounds. They also can receive $50,000 and more in grants. Obano said Scale will help them expand into new markets.
BFN further offers a career advancement program that trains and connects the BFN network's best-performing talent with companies that want to hire them. He noted that sometimes founders in his program realize they would rather work for someone else than build their own companies. BFN awards grants to companies to hire from this talent pool.
Additionally, the BE Her program addresses the unique challenges Black women entrepreneurs face.
Over the past five years, BFN's programming has served more than 15,000 people. Success stories include OneCliq, an AI-powered culture-context insights engine co-founded by siblings Nathan Knight and Tanika McLeod, which Dig Insights acquired in July 2025.
Knight and McLeod now mentor for BFN's programs and have also invested in some of its companies.
BFN has more than $200 million in financial value, and Obano said this reflects its companies' revenues and the funds they've raised.
Looking ahead, he added that a Black Founders Fund is in the works to create more funding pathways, and he is in talks with well-resourced, credible universities to replicate the work they have done with the University of Toronto.

Why Is Dell Technologies (DELL) Up 9.3% Since Last Earnings Report?
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Dell Technologies (DELL). Shares have added about 9.3% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.
Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Dell Technologies due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for Dell Technologies Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
DELL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong AI Demand Aids Revenue Growth
Dell Technologies reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $7.04 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 41.65%. The company reported earnings of $2.32 per share in the year-ago quarter.
Revenues surged 58% to $46.97 billion and beat the consensus mark by 8.57%. Broad-based infrastructure demand drove the quarterly results, while AI server orders reached a record $60.9 billion.
DELL's ISG Growth Accelerates Across the Portfolio
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) revenues jumped 89% year over year to a record $31.78 billion. AI-optimized server revenues doubled to $16.4 billion, while traditional servers and networking revenues surged 122% year over year to $10.53 billion. Dell exited the quarter with $95 billion of AI backlog, while its opportunity pipeline remained multiples of backlog.
Storage revenues increased 26% year over year to $4.85 billion as Dell IP demand grew above the market for a sixth consecutive quarter.
ISG operating income jumped 225% year over year to $4.78 billion, with operating margin expanding 620 basis points (bps) on a year-over-year basis to 15%. Dell also said its AI customer base surpassed 6,500 across neocloud, sovereign and enterprise customers.
Dell's Server Refresh Opportunity Supports Demand
Dell said traditional server demand reflects data-center modernization, security and resiliency requirements, and rising CPU needs tied to AI and agentic workloads. The company still has roughly 1.2 million installed assets running 14th-generation or older servers, leaving a sizable refresh opportunity as customers upgrade infrastructure.
Dell also highlighted significant consolidation benefits from newer systems. Seventeenth-generation servers can replace five to seven legacy servers, while 18th-generation systems can replace up to 13. The newer platforms also offer higher processing density and better power efficiency, supporting modernization even as industry supply remains constrained.
Dell's CSG Posts Broad-Based Revenue Growth
Client Solutions Group (CSG) revenues increased 20% year over year to $15.03 billion. Commercial revenues rose 22% year over year to $13.19 billion, marking the eighth straight quarter of growth, while consumer revenues advanced 7% to $1.84 billion. Demand grew across all regions and verticals, led by large-enterprise PC refresh activity.
CSG operating income increased 42% year over year to $1.14 billion. The operating margin improved 120 bps to 7.6%, supported by pricing discipline and greater scale.
Dell said it will continue balancing demand with product availability as it pursues profitable share gains in the client business.
DELL Expands Profitability Through Scale and Mix
Non-GAAP gross margin rose 78% year over year to $9.93 billion, while the gross margin improved to 21.1% from 18.7%.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 22% year over year to $4 billion but fell to 8.5% of revenues from 11% a year earlier, reflecting meaningful operating leverage.
That expense leverage helped non-GAAP operating income surge 160% year over year to $5.93 billion. The operating margin expanded to 12.6% from 7.7%, aided by higher revenue scale, pricing discipline and improved storage profitability.
Management tied part of the storage improvement to a higher mix of Dell IP products and better rates across solutions.
DELL Delivers Strong Cash Flow and Capital Returns
As of July 31, 2026, DELL has $14.248 billion in cash and investments and a core leverage ratio of 0.8 times. The company reported $14.062 billion in cash and investments as of May 1.
Cash flow from operations totaled $2.23 billion in the reported quarter, while adjusted free cash flow reached $8.15 billion.
Dell returned a record $4.3 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, underscoring the cash generation from higher profitability and revenue scale. Dell repurchased 9.5 million shares at an average price of $401 per share and paid a quarterly dividend of about 63 cents per share.
Dell Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue and Earnings Outlook
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Dell expects revenues of $49 billion, plus or minus $500 million, and non-GAAP earnings of $6.50 per share, plus or minus 10 cents.
DELL expects ISG revenues to grow roughly 145%, supported by about $19 billion in AI server revenues, while CSG revenues are expected to rise roughly 15%.

Why Is Dell Technologies (DELL) Reworking Its AI Strategy Under John Roese?
Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) Chief AI Officer John Roese has been recognized by TIME for reshaping the firm's artificial intelligence strategy.
Roese has led a consolidation of Dell's AI projects, bringing fragmented efforts under a unified framework focused on enterprise use cases.
The refocused approach includes generative AI search tools and autonomous AI agents aimed at efficiency, cost control, and faster deployment cycles.
TIME's recognition of Roese's AI overhaul at Dell is an important shift to weigh alongside the rest of our assessment of the company. Take a look at 3 warning signs we have identified for Dell Technologies.
For a wider lens on where AI buildout is heading, compare Dell's approach with the broader set of companies building core infrastructure through 84 AI infrastructure stocks.
Dell Technologies operates as a global tech supplier that designs and supports hardware, software, and integrated solutions across multiple regions. A tighter AI roadmap directly affects how its servers, storage, and enterprise services can plug into customers' existing infrastructure decisions.
Does the team leading Dell Technologies have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.
What exactly has John Roese changed inside Dell Technologies?
Roese cut Dell's AI portfolio from about 900 projects to fewer than 100 and tied each one to a hard outcome such as revenue, profit, cost, or regulatory risk. That kind of pruning reduces duplicated effort and pushes product teams to focus on AI tools, like search and autonomous agents, that have clear payoffs for enterprise customers.
Does this recognition change the Dell Technologies Narrative investors have been using?
The Narrative already leans on rising enterprise AI demand, more tailored offerings, and a mix shift toward higher margin storage and services. Roese's AI reset lines up with that, because it concentrates resources on enterprise AI workloads that can support revenue visibility while still leaving the long running risks around hardware commoditization and the cyclical PC business in place.
See how these catalysts shape Dell Technologies' path to a $564 fair value.
What should investors watch next to judge whether this AI refocus is working?
The clearest test is how Dell's AI heavy infrastructure and services performance compares with the analyst framework that points to revenue of about US$265.3b and earnings of roughly US$20.5b by 2029. Progress toward those earnings and margin assumptions will indicate whether this refocused AI playbook is aligning with the financial profile analysts have mapped out.
One more Dell Technologies check before you even think about touching the stock
Before you treat Dell Technologies as just an AI story, there is a quieter question to answer about what its future cash generation suggests the whole business might be worth versus today's share price. Find out exactly what Dell Technologies is worth today based on its cash flows.

Dell Technologies (DELL) Stock Fair Value Edges Higher As Analysts Split On AI Outlook
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 1:13 PM CDT 4 min read
The fair value estimate for Dell Technologies has been updated to US$594.16 from US$579.36, reflecting a modest change in how analysts are framing the stock today. This shift sits against a split backdrop, where some analysts see Dell as a key AI hardware beneficiary, while others are more cautious as valuations move higher and enterprise spending expectations build. As you read on, you will see how this evolving narrative may shape the way you track Dell Technologies from here.
Stay updated as the Fair Value for Dell Technologies shifts by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio. Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on Dell Technologies.
Several firms, including Evercore ISI, Mizuho, JPMorgan, Bernstein and BofA, have lifted Dell Technologies price targets into a US$600 to US$650 range or higher, reflecting confidence in AI driven infrastructure demand, high margin storage attach and what they describe as strong execution.
Truist and TD Cowen highlight Dell Technologies AI server backlog, with Truist pointing to what it calls record AI server backlog and TD Cowen citing US$95b of AI server backlog levered to major neoclouds, which they see as adding visibility to longer term AI oriented forecasts.
RBC Capital and Deutsche Bank point to Dell Technologies broad portfolio across compute, storage, PCs and servers, combined with its supply chain and consumption models, as support for continued share gains and a role in large scale AI buildouts.
Barclays recently downgraded Dell Technologies to Equal Weight from Overweight and trimmed its price target to US$574 from US$603, citing richer valuations across IT hardware stocks tied to enterprise spending and limited evidence so far of what it calls a meaningful AI inflection.
Morgan Stanley and UBS keep more neutral stances, flagging richer expectations, questions around the durability of pricing and margin capture in infrastructure solutions and what they see as tougher near term setups for enterprise hardware stocks after a period of strong AI related enthusiasm.
Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. Head to the Simply Wall St Community to discover more perspectives!
We've flagged 3 risks for Dell Technologies. See which could impact your investment.
Dell Technologies reported fiscal second quarter 2027 revenue of US$47b, including about US$16.4b from AI optimized servers and a US$95b AI server backlog, and updated full year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to around US$192b.
The company expanded its AI Data Platform with a Unified Semantic Layer, an Enterprise Knowledge Graph and Knowledge Agents that are designed to support governed enterprise data for AI workloads using Nvidia acceleration and multi tenant PowerScale storage.
Dell Technologies launched new AI focused Windows PCs and workstations, including the XPS 16 Creator Edition, Dell Creator Edition Desktop and Dell Pro Precision with GB300, aimed at local AI development and always on AI agents.
Dell agreed to participate in an AI data center project in Japan of more than US$15b with JERA and RHAELM, providing rack scale computing for a planned 400 MW facility near Chiba that is targeted to start operations around 2028.
How This Changes the Fair Value For Dell Technologies

Future P/E multiple updated to 20.60x from 20.48x.
Discount rate adjusted to 8.75% from 8.84%.

The Sunnyvale facility brings TSMC, Intel, Samsung and others under one roof to cut chip development cycles by at least 30%
Silicon Valley is home to companies worth trillions of dollars apiece. Apple, Alphabet and Meta all live there.
What the region has rarely had is the heavy industrial machinery behind those fortunes. Most chip facilities now operate overseas or in other states, and the local skyline is mostly modest office parks.
Applied Materials is trying to change that. On October 12, 2026, the company inaugurated its $5 billion Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in Sunnyvale, California.
The facility is described as the largest investment in advanced semiconductor R&D in the United States.
The building covers 600,000 square feet. Nearly four acres of that is cleanroom space, the ultra-controlled environment where chip processes are developed and tested.
Construction took more than six million hours of labor.
The headline goal is speed. Applied Materials aims to shrink the traditional semiconductor development cycle by at least 30%.
The mechanism is collaboration. Today, the path from a new chipmaking idea to a working production process tends to move step by step. An equipment maker builds a tool, a chipmaker tests it, researchers study the results, and the loop repeats.
The EPIC Center is designed to run those steps in parallel. Chipmakers, equipment manufacturers and academic researchers can work on the same problems at the same site, at the same time.

Broadcom joins as an innovation partner. Stanford and UC Berkeley are among the academic institutions involved.
The facility is also expected to improve access to mature technologies through faster collaboration.
The timing is tied to surging demand for AI capabilities. AI workloads require increasingly complex, high-performance chips, and the industry faces mounting pressure to deliver them faster.
Applied Materials CEO Gary Dickerson has stressed the need for integrated development processes. His argument is that the old, sequential approach cannot keep up with the complexity AI-driven chip demand now requires.
For investors watching the semiconductor sector, the clearest signal is coordination. When TSMC, Intel, Samsung, SK hynix and Micron all sign on as founding partners, it suggests the industry sees shared R&D infrastructure as worth the competitive awkwardness.
If the center delivers on the 30% target, the payoff could be faster time-to-market for advanced chips.
Because the work targets technologies three to four generations ahead of current production, participants may get a head start on processes that competitors outside the partnership will only see later.
For Applied Materials specifically, the move positions the company as more than a toolmaker. It becomes the host of the industry’s shared lab, which could deepen its relationships with the biggest customers in the business.
The things to watch from here: how quickly partner projects move through the facility, whether additional companies or universities join, and whether the promised speedup shows up in actual product roadmaps rather than press materials.

As the demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to accelerate, investors often weigh the merits of equipment providers against those of chip designers. Choosing between Applied Materials (AMAT -1.97%) and Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) requires a close look at two very different roles in the global supply chain.
Applied Materials provides the essential tools used to fabricate advanced chips, while Broadcom designs specialized silicon and infrastructure software. They are being compared because both are vital players in the artificial intelligence build-out, though they operate at different stages of the production cycle. This comparison evaluates their financial health and market positioning.
Applied Materials sells the complex machinery that other companies use to build chips, serving major foundries and memory makers. The expansion of global data centers has kept semiconductor stocks at the center of many growth-focused portfolios. Applied Materials maintains a highly concentrated customer base, with two customers accounting for approximately 19% and 15% of net revenue in fiscal 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, though it includes a deep partnership with Intel (INTC -0.37%) on next-generation manufacturing.
In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $28.4 billion, an increase of 4.4% over the prior year. Net income was roughly $7 billion, which resulted in a net margin of close to 24.7%. This performance highlights the company's steady financial position in its latest annual report, filed for the period ending in late 2025.
As of its October 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.3. The current ratio, which indicates the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, was nearly 2.6. Free cash flow, which is cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, was approximately $5.7 billion for the fiscal period.
Broadcom provides a mix of specialized chips and infrastructure software. Its chips are essential for cloud data centers and high-end smartphones, while its software segment offers cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure. The company maintains major agreements including a $200 billion memorandum of understanding with Samsung and a $30 billion chip commitment with Apple (AAPL -1.00%).
In fiscal 2025, revenue grew by about 23.9% to nearly $63.9 billion. The company reported net income of approximately $23.1 billion for the year, resulting in a net margin of roughly 36.2%. This was a significant increase in profitability compared to the net income reported in the prior year.
As of its November 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.8, while its current ratio was nearly 1.7. Free cash flow reached roughly $26.9 billion for the year. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 27.5% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Applied Materials faces volatility inherent in the semiconductor industry and heavy geographic concentration. Nearly 89% of its revenue comes from outside the United States, making it sensitive to international trade shifts. Complex export controls, particularly regarding sales to China, remain a persistent challenge for the equipment maker. The company also paid a $252 million settlement in 2026 for export violations involving Semiconductor Manufacturing International.
Broadcom carries substantial indebtedness, which totaled nearly $67.12 billion as of late 2025. Its customer base is also highly concentrated, with a notable reliance on Alphabet for certain revenue streams. The company is navigating intense regulatory scrutiny, including antitrust challenges in the EU related to its VMware operations. Integration risks from large acquisitions and a legal dispute with AT&T (T +0.95%) also factor into its risk profile.
Broadcom is cheaper by forward P/E, which tracks future earnings estimates, while Applied Materials leads on P/S ratio, which measures market cap against 12-month sales.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Broadcom looks kind of expensive to me here. Applied Materials seems relatively boring; 4.4% growth isn't anything to write home about, but I think the valuation reflects that. On the other hand, Broadcom stock has outperformed Applied Materials by over 400 percentage points over the past 10 years, so its elevated valuation may also be justified.
On the other, other hand, smart investors know past performance is no indication of future results, and as a naturally conservative investor, I look at these companies' vastly different market caps and wonder which has the room for more growth. My guess is Applied Materials isn't going to knock your socks off, but it's outpaced the S&P 500 handily over the past 10 years. Furthermore, Broadcom seems closer to a ceiling than Applied Materials; the law of large numbers will make it harder for the former to keep posting those impressive revenue growth rates. I prefer Applied Materials.

Semiconductor equipment stocks are giving back ground after a strong year powered by artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT | AMAT Price Prediction) stock is at $461.91, down 7% in afternoon trading, a pullback that still leaves it up 80% year to date. Selling is greatest among the companies that build chipmaking tools, a narrow corner of the chip trade.
Meanwhile, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) stock is trading at $297.04, down 4%, a smaller decline than the one hitting Applied Materials stock. Likewise, KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) shares are slipping 4% to $182.44, keeping pace with Lam Research stock.
Chip stocks as a group are holding up far better. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is down 1%. Over in large-cap tech, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.5%, a much softer reading than anything in the equipment group.
Applied Materials Gives Back Gains After EPIC Center Debut
Applied Materials stock is giving back part of a large advance, with the decline running alongside its equipment peers. One session earlier, the company unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization Center, known as the EPIC Center, at its Sunnyvale campus. Management describes the site as the world’s largest facility for collaborative semiconductor process and equipment research. Applied Materials expects capital spending there to scale to approximately $5 billion as customer projects begin.
A leading chipmaker joined the center as a founding partner, giving the project a strong start. Recent results also support the longer-term story. In August, Applied Materials reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $3.50 against a $3.39 estimate and guided Q4 FY2026 revenue to about $10.25 billion.
Equipment Makers Slide Harder Than the Broader Chip Group
All three equipment names carry large gains into the pullback, with Lam Research stock up 74% year to date and KLA stock up 51%. Each is falling several times harder than the semiconductor fund that holds them, a split that points at fabrication spending intentions, because the iShares fund also owns chip designers and foundries and its decline serves as broad sector context.
The EPIC Center commits capital to exactly the advanced-node and packaging work that AI buildouts require, and it ties major customers to Applied Materials earlier in the design cycle. In Q3 FY2026, U.S. customers accounted for 15% of Applied Materials’ revenue, while China fell to 28% from 35%. Looking further out, Applied Materials’ chief executive stated in the August results release, “Based on the increased demand visibility we are receiving from our customers, we expect another strong growth year for Applied Materials in 2027.”
Yet, equipment orders are discretionary, and a stock carrying a year-to-date gain of that size has a long way to fall whenever that spending is questioned. Policy adds another layer of risk, since China still made up a large share of Applied Materials’ revenue last quarter. The AI boom puts Applied Materials (AMAT -1.97%) and SK Hynix (SKHY -2.16%) at the center of the chip race. Choosing between the equipment giant and the memory leader depends on your goals for 2026.
Applied Materials provides the essential tools used to build semiconductors, while SK hynix produces the memory chips that store and move data. Both companies are critical to the global supply chain, yet they operate in different niches. This comparison explores their financial health and market positions to help you determine which stock better fits your strategy.
Applied Materials leads the materials engineering sector by providing the equipment and services required to deposit, shape, and analyze materials with atomic precision for chipmaking. It recently expanded its collaboration with Intel (INTC -0.37%) to advance AI technologies and maintains a strategic partnership with TSMC to meet growing foundry demand. Two specific partners account for approximately 19% and 15% of revenue, and such customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

Net income for the period was approximately $7.0 billion, resulting in a net margin of close to 24.7%. This figure reflects a slight decrease from the 26.4% net margin recorded in FY 2024, yet it remains significantly higher than the levels seen in FY 2023.

This approach focuses on high-bandwidth memory and next-generation storage for data centers to capture a larger share of global digital infrastructure spending.

When comparing Applied Materials and SK Hynix, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

Its operating margin has averaged 30% over the last five years. SK Hynix, by contrast, has averaged around 21%. However, that average is dragged down by years of losses in 2023 and 2024. In summary, it's appropriate for growth-oriented investors to give both of these stocks strong consideration. However, in a head-to-head matchup, SK Hynix comes out ahead due to its superior growth rate, lower forward P/E multiple, and excellent operating margin.

Broadcom vs. Applied Materials: Which Buybacks Are Actually Shrinking the Share Count?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:57 PM CDT 3 min read
Broadcom and Applied Materials both generate cash and repurchase shares, but shareholders ultimately own a fraction of a business. Our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade makes that distinction important: buyback spending is useful only in the context of issuance, the price paid and the cash needed to sustain growth. Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) offers custom silicon, networking and software exposure. Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT) sells semiconductor-manufacturing equipment and services. They are different routes into AI-related investment, compared here on shareholder participation in cash growth.
Broadcom vs. Applied Materials: Which Buybacks Are Actually Shrinking the Share Count?
Close-up of Silicon Die are being Extracted from Semiconductor Wafer and Attached to Substrate by Pick and Place Machine. Computer Chip Manufacturing at Fab. Semiconductor Packaging Process.
A repurchase bill is not a net reduction
Broadcom spent $8.450 billion on repurchases over its first nine fiscal months. Yet weighted-average basic shares rose from 4.705 billion to 4.752 billion year over year, about 1.0%. Applied spent $1.177 billion over its first nine fiscal months, while weighted-average basic shares fell from 807 million to 794 million, about 1.6%.
The fiscal periods also differ slightly. They nevertheless show why dividing repurchases by market capitalization can overstate the ownership benefit: issuance and timing affect the actual denominator.
Applied delivered the more favorable net share-count direction in these reported periods. That does not prove its repurchases created more value. Buying overvalued shares can destroy value even when the number outstanding falls. Our Lam-Applied cash-coverage comparison tests a different prerequisite: whether payouts were supported by cash after investment.
Cash compensation and stock compensation both matter
Broadcom reported $6.287 billion of stock-based compensation in the nine-month cash-flow reconciliation; Applied reported $545 million. Stock compensation is added back in operating cash flow because it is noncash in that period, but it can dilute shareholders or require repurchases to offset issuance. It should not be mistaken for a costless source of cash.
Their nine-month operating cash after direct capital expenditure was $31.937 billion and $3.580 billion. As a conservative accounting-cost sensitivity, subtracting reported stock compensation leaves $25.650 billion and $3.035 billion. This is not GAAP cash flow or the cash actually needed to neutralize dilution; grant values, vesting and future repurchase prices differ.
If company-wide cash grew 10% while shares increased 1%, cash per share would rise about 8.9%. With shares falling 1.6%, the same cash growth would produce about 11.8% per-share growth.
At October 16 equity values, trailing cash after capital spending cost about 40 times for Broadcom and 58 times for Applied. Broadcom's lower multiple and stronger cash generation can outweigh modest dilution, while Applied's shrinking denominator cannot alone justify its price.
For investors weighing the chip-design alternative, our Nvidia-Broadcom comparison connects the cash-flow price with the growth assumptions behind each business.
Q2 2026 hedge-fund holders fell to 170 from 173 for Broadcom and to 137 from 138 for Applied. Fisher increased Broadcom shares 3%; Coatue reduced Applied shares 20%. Broadcom's September 30 short interest was 1.16% of float.
Applied currently shows the better net share-count direction. The lasting investment test is cash growth per share after competitive reinvestment, rather than the largest repurchase announcement or the smallest stock-compensation adjustment.

Applied Materials declined to provide an industry spending forecast at its investor day, and shares fell 6.69% in a single session. The weakness hit the whole group, but Applied took the most damage. Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) fell 2.73% and KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) dropped 3.22% on the same day, while the S&P 500 slipped just 0.01%.
Analysts Keep Raising Estimates as the Stock Falls
Analysts are focused on to AI-driven demand that management says stretches years out. Applied Materials Bull and Bear Cases Hinge on the 2027 Spending Outlook
Shares look more compelling if DRAM and advanced packaging ramp as guided and fiscal Q4 lands near $10.25 billion. That keeps the $18.4658 fiscal 2027 EPS path intact and makes a forward multiple near 23x look reasonable for this growth rate. A clear 2027 spending outlook would also remove the uncertainty behind this week’s drop.
The bear case gains weight if clean room shortages cap shipments, export controls squeeze China sales, or the investor day silence signals a weaker 2027 than analysts model. China already declined to 28% of revenue from 35%.
On balance, the data leans positive. Estimates are rising, guidance points higher, and the stock trades 37.2% off its high. The missing forecast is a real yellow flag, so management’s 2027 outlook is the next data point to keep an eye on.

Semiconductor manufacturers are planning huge expansions over the next few years to meet the booming demand for AI chips. Memory chipmakers hesitated to expand at first, but now have hundreds of billions of dollars worth of new facilities set to go into chip production starting next year. Meanwhile, the largest third-party chip manufacturer in the world, TSMC, has continuously raised its capital expenditure budget as it aims to keep up with demand.
While there are multiple ways to invest in the growing demand for semiconductor production, one of the best is to move up the supply chain to silicon wafer fabrication equipment makers. Two of the biggest companies in the space are ASML (ASML -0.99%) and Applied Materials (AMAT -1.97%). Both are excellent companies with strong competitive advantages, but if you can only choose one, which stock is worth buying today?

Applied Materials: A diversified approach
Applied Materials holds a broad portfolio of equipment and maintains a very impressive market share across the group. Its deposition equipment (which adds conductive or insulating materials to a silicon wafer) is one of its fastest-growing businesses in 2026, even as it maintains a leading market share. The company is also seeing strong growth across etching, process diagnostics and control, and its thermals and treatments segments.
The diversified approach comes with a significant benefit. Applied Materials can sell combined offerings to customers by integrating different processes into a single piece of equipment. That can save its customers up-front costs as well as floor space, increasing production capacity. Over time, Applied Materials has come to work more closely with its customers, which has given it better insight into their needs.

Of course, maintaining a broad portfolio of market-leading equipment also requires significant investment in research and development (R&D). Applied Materials' R&D budget is significantly larger than its competitors' with much narrower product lines. That said, Applied Materials also earns revenue capable of supporting that R&D. Its operating margin of 31% is below that of competitors like KLA and Lam Research, but that's largely due to the lower-gross-margin profile of deposition equipment, which accounts for a larger share of Applied Materials' revenue.
In fact, the large R&D budget could ultimately benefit Applied Materials, as it enables the company to innovate quickly and stay ahead of competitors. Its leading position in deposition could enable it to gain market share in other equipment, especially through its integrated solutions. As a result, operating margin should expand over time, leading to very strong earnings growth.
ASML makes lithography machines that print circuits on silicon wafers. It's an absolutely dominant force with about 90% of the total market for lithography equipment and technological capabilities that are years, if not decades, ahead of the next-closest competitor.
That lead is crucial, especially in the current period of rapidly expanding production capacity. ASML's machines last for up to 30 years. That means competitors hoping to catch up to ASML will miss out on sales during the current investment cycle, while ASML benefits from a growing installed base to service each year. ASML is working to take advantage of the situation by expanding its own capacity by 30% next year and a further 30% in 2028.

The move should produce very strong earnings growth for the business as it sells more high-end machines, which carry higher margins and higher service revenue. Even memory chipmakers (which are much less technologically advanced than logic chipmakers) are looking to use ASML's most advanced equipment. The expanded scale should also support higher operating margins.
Which stock should you buy?
Both companies are set to experience very strong growth over the next few years as sales climb and margins expand. ASML's dominant position in lithography means it can charge premium prices for its equipment, limited only by its customers' ability to produce meaningful returns on the capital invested. With the rising prices for both memory and logic chips fueled by AI demand, that trend is working very much in favor of ASML.
However, Applied Materials has the opportunity to expand its market share of higher-margin equipment as manufacturers expand capacity over the next few years by cross-selling and integrating equipment across its broad portfolio. That could ultimately position it for much stronger revenue growth over the long run, as its share gains tend to be sticky. There's no room for ASML to increase its market share.
The two stocks trade for similar forward P/E ratios around 40 times expectations over the next 12 months. If you go out to 2028, ASML trades for 23 times analysts' earnings-per-share expectations for the year, while Applied Materials trades for 21 times expectations. Given Applied Materials' ability to maintain a higher growth rate over the long run after the current investment cycle, it looks like the better buy right now.

Among recent announcements, the extended collaboration with Intel around the EPIC Center looks most relevant. Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:39 PM CDT 4 min read
Applied Materials Stock Fell 21% in 8 Straight Sessions. Here's What Its 2030 Targets Mean for Shares ©@Kittipong Jirasukhanont from PhonlamaiPhoto's Images via Canva, @Jakub Pabis from Pexels via Canva
What Happened?
"We're not going to give a specific WFE forecast today," Applied Materials (AMAT) CEO Gary Dickerson told investors at the company's SEMICON West breakfast on Oct. 13, 2026. He followed it with "tremendous confidence" that computing demand would keep growing. Even so, reports from BigGo and Dow Jones tied the stock's extra decline to the missing number. Shares closed down 6.69% at $464.24 that day and fell to $430.01 by Oct. 15, an eighth straight losing session.
The sector was already sliding. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had dropped for six sessions by Oct. 13, and memory stocks fell hard that day after a report on China's ChangXin Memory. Lam Research (LRCX), KLA (KLAC) and ASML (ASML) lost 2.6% to 3.5%, about half of Applied's decline or less.
The 2030 Margin Math Does Not Depend on a WFE Number
The breakfast did deliver targets, laid out in Applied's investor relations materials: a 54% non-GAAP gross margin and a 40% non-GAAP operating margin by calendar 2030. CFO Brice Hill put the current gross margin at about 50%. TIKR's fiscal 2026 consensus shows an EBIT margin of around 33%.
Hill then gave the bridge. "We'll expect to get 4 additional points on the gross margin. And we will expect to achieve 200 to 300 basis points in operating leverage," he said. He credited AI automation in corporate functions for the second part. The pieces add up: around 33%, plus 4 points, plus 2 to 3 points lands near 40%.
He expects about 100 basis points of gross margin gain a year, though not in a straight line. He also said Applied is raising prices, partly to cover costs such as fuel and rare earths.
Services may be the most overlooked target. Applied Global Services generated $6.385 billion in fiscal 2025, and Applied targets more than $12 billion by calendar 2030. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon asked why connected chambers rising from 37,000 to 90,000 only yields mid-teens growth. Hill answered that the installed base grows 5% to 10% a year, and new products supply the rest.
Applied Materials Global Services Operating Revenue (TIKR)
A Cheaper Multiple, a Target Cut and the China Math
Since Jan. 25, 2026, Applied's NTM normalized EPS estimate has risen 83% to $17.61. Over the same stretch, its forward P/E ratio fell to 24.41x from 33.48x.
China is the clearest reason for caution. Head of Investor Relations Michael Sullivan said Applied could sell into 100% of China's equipment market in the early 2020s, then 90%, and "closer to 70%" in 2025. Hill said the 2030 share-gain target still assumes growth in restricted Chinese accounts under current trade rules. China supplied $8.529 billion of Applied's $28.368 billion in fiscal 2025 revenue, about 30%.
Evercore ISI cut its target to $590 from $700 on Oct. 14 and kept an Outperform rating. Cantor Fitzgerald's C.J. Muse reiterated an $850 target on Oct. 13, about 34% above TIKR's $632.28 Street mean. TIKR shows 29 Buy, 4 Outperform, and 7 Hold ratings. Fiscal Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.50 beat estimates, but GAAP EPS of $3.17 missed the $3.44 estimate.
Applied Materials NTM Price / Normalized Earnings (P/E) (TIKR)
Applied Materials Advanced Valuation Model (TIKR)
The mid case is a scenario, not a forecast. It assumes around 15% annual revenue growth, a net margin near 33% and a slightly shrinking P/E. Applied's own targets point a little higher: a 40% operating margin taxed at management's estimated 15% rate leaves about 34%, before interest income.
Management expects leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging to supply about 75% of equipment spending growth through 2030. The main risk is uneven timing, with Hill flagging supply chain "pinch points that have to be managed." Margins above 54%, which Cantor considers conservative, are the upside. A spending pause that compresses the multiple before earnings catch up is the downside.
Applied reports fiscal Q4 results on Nov. 12. The Street expects about $10.30 billion in revenue and $4.06 in adjusted EPS, inside guidance of $9.75 billion to $10.75 billion.
Gross margin is the line to watch against management's 50.4% guide. Meeting it is the first data point on the road to 54%. A miss would weaken the 2030 bridge at its first step.

Shares of Applied Materials (AMAT) have gained 10.2% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $464.24, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $647.09 indicates a potential upside of 39.4%.
The average comprises 33 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $515.00 to a high of $900.00, with a standard deviation of $92.03. While the lowest estimate indicates an increase of 10.9% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 93.9% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is a much-coveted metric for investors, solely banking on this metric to make an investment decision may not be wise at all. That's because the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable.
But, for AMAT, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.
Zacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for AMAT
Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
Here's Why There Could be Plenty of Upside Left in AMAT
Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
For the current year, one estimate has moved higher over the last 30 days compared to no negative revision. As a result, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has increased 0.2%.
Moreover, AMAT currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much AMAT could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.
